ringworm.title: Home Care for Ringworm
remedies: **Apple Cider Vinegar:** Apply a 50/50 solution of ACV and water to the affected area with a cotton ball a few times a day.
**Antifungal Shampoo:** Bathe your dog with a medicated antifungal shampoo available from pet stores.
**Keep the Area Clean and Dry:** Moisture helps the fungus thrive. Ensure the affected skin is kept dry.
ringworm.disclaimer: ⚠️ **Disclaimer:** These are supportive home remedies. Ringworm is contagious to humans and other pets. Always consult a veterinarian for a proper diagnosis and treatment plan.

dermatitis.title: Home Care for Dermatitis
remedies: **Oatmeal Baths:** Soothe itchy skin with a colloidal oatmeal bath. Grind plain oatmeal into a fine powder and add it to warm water.
**Coconut Oil:** Applying a small amount of virgin coconut oil can moisturize dry, irritated skin.
**Identify and Remove Allergens:** Dermatitis is often caused by allergens. Try to identify and eliminate potential triggers from your dog's environment or diet.
dermatitis.disclaimer: ⚠️ **Disclaimer:** If the skin is broken, oozing, or does not improve, please see a veterinarian immediately to prevent secondary infections.

fungal_infections.title: Home Care for Fungal Infections
remedies: **Medicated Shampoos:** Use shampoos containing ingredients like ketoconazole or miconazole as recommended by a vet.
**Keep Skin Dry:** Fungi thrive in moist environments. Make sure to thoroughly dry your dog after baths, especially between skin folds.
fungal_infections.disclaimer: ⚠️ **Disclaimer:** Fungal infections can be persistent. A veterinarian's diagnosis is crucial to ensure you are using the correct treatment.

demodicosis.title: Home Care for Demodicosis (Mange)
remedies: **Boost the Immune System:** Demodicosis is often linked to a weak immune system. Ensure your dog has a high-quality diet and low stress.
**Medicated Baths:** A veterinarian may prescribe special shampoos or dips to help kill the mites.
**Do Not Use Home Remedies without Vet Approval:** Treating mange requires specific medication. Unapproved treatments can worsen the condition.
demodicosis.disclaimer: ⚠️ **Disclaimer:** Demodectic mange requires a veterinary diagnosis and prescription treatment. Do not attempt to treat it at home without professional guidance.

hypersensitivity.title: Home Care for Hypersensitivity (Allergies)
remedies: **Avoid the Allergen:** The most effective treatment is to identify and remove the source of the allergic reaction (e.g., certain foods, pollen, dust mites).
**Soothing Baths:** Use a hypoallergenic or oatmeal-based shampoo to calm irritated skin.
**Omega-3 Fatty Acids:** Supplements like fish oil can help improve the skin barrier and reduce inflammation.
hypersensitivity.disclaimer: ⚠️ **Disclaimer:** Severe allergic reactions may require medication from a veterinarian. Consult a vet to develop a management plan.

healthy.title: Maintaining Healthy Skin
remedies: **Regular Grooming:** Brushing regularly removes dead hair and skin cells and distributes natural oils.
**Balanced Diet:** Ensure your dog is on a high-quality diet rich in omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids.
**Flea and Tick Prevention:** Use regular preventative treatments to avoid skin irritation from parasites.
healthy.disclaimer: This advice is for general wellness. If you notice any changes in your dog's skin, consult a vet.
